reasons: Relationship checks do not run when fields are changed later.
Uses an older validation style that may print warnings or need updates.

terms.meaning: a library that checks data types and ranges when objects are created
a rule that runs automatically when an object is created and rejects bad values
a fixed list of allowed choices, such as low, medium or high
a unique code that identifies one item so other items can refer to it
a standard text layout for dates and times

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and file purpose
sections.what: Brings in the type tools, the validation library, date handling and the enum helper. The header says the file holds the data models for the Proposal Builder.
sections.why: Needed for the checks and defaults used by every class below.
sections.watch_out: The validator and class config styles are from an older version of the validation library, so an upgrade may change how they behave.

sections.name: RiskLevel
sections.title: Risk level choices
sections.what: Lists the three risk levels for activities: low, medium and high.
sections.why: Keeps risk values to a known set of words.
sections.watch_out: The values are stored as plain text, so the app must send exactly these spellings.

sections.name: GovernanceFrequency
sections.title: Governance meeting frequency choices
sections.what: Lists the allowed meeting rhythms: weekly, biweekly, monthly and milestone.
sections.why: Keeps meeting frequency to known options.
sections.watch_out: The workstream default is monthly, so a workstream with no stated frequency will show monthly meetings.

sections.name: Evidence
sections.title: Evidence record
sections.what: Stores one piece of past proposal text that the search found, with its source file, document type, similarity score, extra details and time of retrieval.
sections.why: Lets the app show where a recommendation came from.
sections.watch_out: The document type is free text described only by a comment, so nothing stops a mistyped value.

sections.name: Activity
sections.title: Activity record
sections.what: Describes one task inside a module: its name, duration between half a week and 20 weeks, outputs, dependencies, resources, risk, critical path flag and start and end weeks. The end week is worked out from the start and duration when the object is created.
sections.why: Lets the plan show the detail below each module.
sections.watch_out: The end week is calculated only once, so changing the start week later leaves the end week out of date. A start week of zero is treated as missing.

sections.name: Module
sections.title: Module record
sections.what: Describes one module inside a workstream: its name, duration, start week, deliverables, activities, dependencies and governance notes. It can report its end week, and it checks that its activities do not add up to much more than its duration.
sections.why: The 1.5 times allowance lets some activities run in parallel, so the total can be larger than the module length. Likely reason: the code comment says the allowance is for parallel work.
sections.watch_out: The allowance is a fixed multiplier, so a large activity list can exceed the module length by up to half and still pass.

sections.name: Workstream
sections.title: Workstream record
sections.what: Describes a top-level workstream: its name, duration between one and 52 weeks, start week, modules, dependencies, parallel work, meeting frequency, workshop flag, confidence and source files. Its check confirms that its modules fit within its duration.
sections.why: Keeps the plan in a shape that the timeline and exports can trust.
sections.watch_out: The module fit check runs only when the workstream is created. Assigning modules later, as the content generator does, skips the check, so an overfull workstream can slip through.

sections.name: DependencyGraph
sections.title: Dependency map
sections.what: Holds the lists of what each workstream, module and activity depends on, plus groups of items that can run in parallel and the critical path items. Two helpers add a dependency and a parallel group.
sections.why: Keeps all the ordering rules in one place, so the timeline and exports read the same information.
sections.watch_out: The parallel group helper compares whole lists, so the same group written in a different order will be added twice.

sections.name: OptimizationResult
sections.title: Timeline optimization result
sections.what: Stores the before and after durations, the weeks saved, adjustments made, parallel blocks, risks, recommendations, the reasoning and a confidence score.
sections.why: Gives a record of what the optimizer changed and why.
sections.watch_out: The weeks saved is a stored number, not a calculation, so it can disagree with the two durations if one changes.

sections.name: AgentReasoning
sections.title: Agent reasoning record
sections.what: Records what one agent did: its name, what it was given, the evidence it used, its steps, its output, its confidence, how long it took and when.
sections.why: Makes the agents' decisions visible so a person can review them.
sections.watch_out: The content generator creates these records but does not save them, so reviews may find nothing.

sections.name: ProjectStructure (part 1)
sections.title: Project record and basic checks
sections.what: The top-level container for a whole proposal: project name, RFP text, workstreams, dependencies, durations, governance, confidence, evidence, reasoning log, timestamps and optimization result. It can find a workstream by its ID and can report the total duration. The total is the optimized duration when it exists, or the latest end week otherwise.
sections.why: Gives the app one object to save, pass around and export.
sections.watch_out: The last modified time is reset every time the object is checked, so it does not show when a person last changed the plan.

sections.name: ProjectStructure: get_module_by_id
sections.title: Finding modules and checking the whole structure
sections.what: Finds a module by its ID across all workstreams. Also runs a full check and returns a list of plain-language problems: duplicate workstream names, duplicate module names, a plan longer than the target, and workstream dependencies that point to missing items.
sections.why: Lets the app flag problems before a proposal is exported.
sections.watch_out: The full check runs only when called, and it does not check module dependencies, so some broken links will not be reported.

sections.name: ExportConfig
sections.title: Export settings
sections.what: Holds the export choices: which extras to include, the color scheme, company and project names, and default lists of Excel sheets and PowerPoint slides.
sections.why: Gives one place to change export options.
sections.watch_out: The exporters in exports.py do not read these settings; they use their own fixed sheet and slide lists, so changing these defaults has no effect on the output.

summary: Defines the shapes of the project data, such as workstreams, modules and activities, and checks that values make sense when they are created.
purpose: Gives the whole app one agreed structure for project data, so that errors are caught early.
why: Likely reason: the AI output is free text, so these checks stop bad values from spreading through the app.
how: Each class is a template with named fields. When a value is given, the library checks its type and range. Some classes also check relationships, such as whether modules fit inside a workstream's duration. Dates and IDs get default values when not supplied.
inputs: Values for each field, usually produced by the agents or read from files.
outputs: Validated objects that other modules read, plus a list of structure problems from ProjectStructure validation.
risks: Relationship checks run only when an object is created, so later edits can break the rules. IDs are built from timestamps, so two items created at the same moment could share an ID. The export settings are not read by the exporters.
debug: If creation fails, read the error text: it names the field and the limit that was broken. For a missing ID, check the ID's timestamp source. For odd duration totals, check whether modules were edited after creation.
